hallucinations.claim: 'A 7B parameter model running on an H100 gains nothing from 4-bit quantization other than a slight speedup'
hallucinations.why: Decode is memory-bandwidth-bound, so a quarter of the bytes gives roughly 2-3x tokens per second on bandwidth-bound decode; 'slight' understates it, though kernel overheads narrow the gain on an H100.

what_went_wrong: Mostly right, but it never states the key rule (a bigger 4-bit model beats a smaller 16-bit one at the same memory), puts the 'negligible loss' threshold at 30B+ when it holds from about 7B, and runs past 'short'.
great_answer_would: Say the bigger-4-bit-beats-smaller-16-bit rule outright, note that 3-bit and below degrade sharply, and cut it to about five sentences.
notes: The memory figures are correct: 70B is ~140 GB at FP16 and ~40 GB at 4-bit, which fits on an A6000 or two 3090/4090s. Mentioning NF4 and the scale/zero-point mechanism is accurate.
